stages.name: Sound start
stages.strands: P— A● T— V● F— C◐
stages.exit: Isolates the first sound of known words; hears same/different words; taps syllables.
stages.why: Phoneme awareness linked to letters is the strongest foundation; this stage is oral, brief and skippable by placement. Initial-sound work comes before rhyme (alliteration is easier).
stages.risk: Japanese kana are mora-based (か = /k/+/a/), so single consonants have no native "address": hold continuous sounds, keep vowels off consonants.

stages.name: Alphabet code
stages.strands: P● A◐ T◐ V● F○ C◐
stages.exit: Decodes unseen CVC pseudo-words from the 26 letters + ff/ll/ss/ck/zz/qu and reads 1–3 sentence ditties.
stages.why: Systematic synthetic phonics: grapheme-phoneme correspondences taught explicitly, blended left to right, spelled by segmenting. Continuous sounds first; confusable letters (b/d, i/e) separated.
stages.risk: Final-consonant vowel insertion ("map" → "mapu"), r/l, b/v, short a/o/u. Contrast packs unlock as both members are taught.

stages.name: Consonant digraphs
stages.ja: ふたもじ ひとおと
stages.strands: P● A○ T◐ V● F◐ C◐
stages.exit: Reads and spells sh/ch/th/ng/nk words; reads 4–8 page stories.
stages.why: A digraph is ONE sound and is taught as one tile (WWC). Introduced while vowels are still all short so each lesson adds one new difficulty.
stages.risk: s/sh, th/s/z (heard as /s/ /z/ or /t/ /d/), final /ŋ/ + inserted /g/ or "gu".

stages.name: Adjacent consonants and first inflections
stages.strands: P● A◐ T◐ V● F◐ C◐
stages.exit: Reads and spells CVCC / CCVC / CCCVC words, and words with -ing / -ed, with no inserted vowels.
stages.why: Clusters are the biggest Japanese-specific hazard (CV syllable habit), so they come EARLY while vowels are short: final clusters before initial (Letters & Sounds Phase 4 logic). Clusters are blended sound by sound, never memorised as chunks.
stages.risk: Epenthetic vowels (hand → "hando", stop → "sutoppu"); r/l inside clusters; -ed as "edo"/"to".

stages.name: Long vowels and other vowels, one spelling each
stages.strands: P● A○ T◐ V● F● C◐
stages.exit: Knows the "simple code" (one spelling per sound); reads short decodable books.
stages.why: One spelling per sound first (limits spelling load; DfE simple-then-complex code). Order suits Japanese phonology: ee/oo (length is a native strength) before the English diphthongs ai/oa/igh/ow/oi.
stages.risk: Flattened diphthongs (cake → "keeki"), i/ee, oo/oo (book/moon), rhotic vowels (ar/or/ur/er/air/ear; accent en-US).

stages.name: Split digraphs, alternative spellings and pronunciations
stages.ja: おなじ おと ちがう つづり
stages.strands: P● A○ T○ V● F● C●
stages.exit: Chooses between alternatives when reading ("tries the other sound") and when spelling; reads short chapter-like texts.
stages.why: Alternatives are added only after the first spelling of that sound is secure. "Try the other sound" needs the word to be known orally, so vocabulary leads. Use ONE term ("split digraph") consistently (DfE fidelity guidance).
stages.risk: Needs oral vocabulary to self-check a decoding attempt; ea/ow/ie/ch have 2+ pronunciations.

stages.name: Multisyllable words and morphology
stages.strands: P● A○ T○ V● F● C●
stages.exit: Decodes 2–3 syllable words; uses prefixes/suffixes to read and spell; handles schwa with "say it, then fix it".
stages.why: Syllable types + division rules turn long words into familiar chunks; affixes carry meaning (morphology absent in Japanese, so explicit teaching).
stages.risk: Stress and weak vowels are unfamiliar (Japanese is mora-timed); plural/past morphology has no Japanese counterpart.

stages.name: Fluency and reading-for-meaning bridge
stages.strands: P◐ A— T— V● F● C●
stages.exit: Rising rate on unpractised text; reads less-controlled texts with comprehension.
stages.why: No new GPCs. After decoding is secure, vocabulary and knowledge limit comprehension (Castles et al.), so the filter switches from "% decodable" to "% of words known orally".
stages.risk: Vocabulary, not code, holds Japanese EFL readers back; connected speech/weak forms are practised in listening only.

oral.label: Oral listening
oral.template: Short games only, no print. Same/different words, first sounds, syllable taps.

code.label: New letter-sound(s)
code.template: Standard 9-step template. 1-2 new GPCs per lesson (max 2 in Stage 1).

digraph.label: Digraph (two letters, one sound)
digraph.template: Standard template; the digraph is ONE tile; minimal-pair listening before print.

cluster.label: Adjacent consonants (no new GPCs)
cluster.template: Stretch-and-segment: one Elkonin box per sound, tiles per letter. Contrast "real word" vs "word + extra vowel" in listening. Blend sound by sound, never as chunks.

inflection.label: Inflection (-ing, -ed)
inflection.template: Word sums (base + ending), ending-sound sort (/t/ /d/ /ɪd/), spell by adding the ending to a known base.

vowel.label: Vowel sound, one spelling
vowel.template: Standard template plus length/glide modelling in the mouth cue; sorts against the nearest short vowel.

split.label: Split digraph
split.template: The two letters are one unit with a gap: tiles with a gap slot. Word chains between short and long vowel words (cap → cape).

altspell.label: Alternative spelling of a known sound
altspell.template: Sound is known; teach another way to write it. Sort by sound, choose the right spelling in a word, keep a "spelling map" of the sound.

altpron.label: Alternative pronunciation of a known spelling
altpron.template: "Try the other sound": decode → check against a word you know → if it is not a word, try the other sound. Needs oral vocabulary.

syllable.label: Syllables
syllable.template: Chop the word, label syllable types, then blend chunk by chunk.

morph.label: Morphology
morph.template: Word sums and word builders: prefix + base + suffix; meaning first, then spelling-change rules.

bridge.label: Bridge to independent reading
bridge.template: Repeated reading, unpractised-passage fluency (personal curve), knowledge-themed text sets, listening library.

checkpoints.name: Alphabet code check
checkpoints.items: 24 items: 12 CVC pseudo-words + 12 real CVC words (choose-from-audio)
checkpoints.pass: >= 85% pseudo-words; every Stage-1 GPC at rung >= 4

checkpoints.name: Digraph check
checkpoints.items: 24 items: sh/ch/th/ng/nk words + 2 short stories (>= 90% word accuracy)

checkpoints.name: Cluster and ending check
checkpoints.items: 24 items: CVCC/CCVC/CCCVC, -ing/-ed; spell 6 words (no inserted vowels)

checkpoints.name: Simple code check
checkpoints.items: 30 items across all Stage 4 vowels + 3 short books

checkpoints.name: Alternatives check
checkpoints.items: 30 items: sort by sound, choose the spelling, "try the other sound" on 10 words
checkpoints.pass: >= 80% on choices; self-corrects on >= 6/10 other-sound words

checkpoints.name: Multisyllable and morphology check
checkpoints.items: 30 items: 2–3 syllable words (real + pseudo), word sums, 2 less-controlled passages
